segments.narration: Four hundred trees in Poland all bend at ninety-degree angles. Planted around 1930, every pine curves horizontally near the roots before reaching straight back toward the sky.
Locals blamed heavy snowfall, magnetic pulls, or World War Two tanks crushing the saplings. Yet the surrounding pine forest grows perfectly straight.
Who forced an entire forest sideways? Historians proved these uniform curves were not a natural miracle—they were engineered.
Local foresters intentionally bent young saplings using wooden frames. They were farming pre-curved timber specifically designed to build curved boat hulls and ox plows.

When World War Two struck in 1939, the town was abandoned before harvest, leaving the trees to grow untouched. If this massive operation was ready for cutting, who was the unknown craftsman behind it?
